references.text: The nations heard about Israel's God and His mighty deeds, which created fear among them - just as the Gibeonites refer to having heard about the Lord.
Reference to God's mighty deeds in Egypt, which the Gibeonites mention they have heard about.
All the peoples of the earth shall see that the name of the Lord is called over Israel - the Gibeonites came precisely because of the name and reputation of the Lord.
Rahab also tells that she has heard what the Lord did in Egypt and how He dried up the Red Sea - the same reason the Gibeonites give.
Solomon's prayer that foreigners should come from distant lands because of the great name of the Lord - a parallel to the Gibeonites' motivation.
The Lord sends people to distant nations who have not heard of His glory - the Gibeonites came from far away because they had heard about the name of the Lord.
The inhabitants of Gibeon heard what Joshua had done to Jericho and Ai, which motivated their plan to seek peace.
